prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a temple was dedicated in 2024.
prompts.text_original: A country where a temple was dedicated in 2024.
prompts.citation: Church temple list (original dedication dates), 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: In 2024 the Church dedicated new temples across the Americas and Asia. Argentina gained two, Salta and Mendoza, and others were dedicated in Puebla Mexico, Salvador Brazil, Lima Peru Los Olivos, Urdaneta Philippines, San Pedro Sula Honduras and Cobán Guatemala. The United States had eight, including Deseret Peak, Taylorsville and Orem in Utah.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Deseret Peak Utah, Taylorsville Utah, Orem Utah and 5 more dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Salta Argentina, Mendoza Argentina dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Lima Peru Los Olivos dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: San Pedro Sula Honduras dedicated in 2024.

prompts.display_text: Pin a continental Western European country (not Luxembourg or a microstate) that recognized the Church, 1952 to 1974
prompts.text_original: After World War II, the Church sought official legal standing from European governments so it could own property and operate freely. One of nine continental Western European countries (Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Belgium or the Netherlands) whose government officially recognized the Church between 1952 and 1974.
prompts.note: Switzerland (1864) and Italy (1993) recognized the Church outside these years, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: In the decades after World War II, Western European governments gave the Church legal standing one by one: France in 1952, West Germany in 1953, Austria and the Netherlands in 1955, Spain in 1968 and Portugal in 1974. Recognition let the Church own meetinghouses, hold meetings openly and bring in missionaries.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: West Germany recognized the Church as a public-law corporation, December 7, 1953.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France registered the Church as a foreign association in September 1952.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Spain officially recognized the Church, October 22, 1968.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Austria granted the Church legal recognition, September 27, 1955.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Netherlands recognized the Church, August 22, 1955, after 19 years of requests.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: David M. Kennedy secured official recognition in Lisbon in 1974.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a place Jesus himself named aloud while teaching, Sodom and Gomorrah aside.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country with a place Jesus himself named aloud when teaching, Sodom and Gomorrah aside
prompts.note: Site is in the West Bank or Gaza; a player may reasonably pin ISR as well.
prompts.summary: Jesus taught with place names his hearers knew. He rebuked Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, set the good Samaritan on the Jericho road, and said Tyre and Sidon would have repented sooner (Matthew 11:21). At Nazareth he pointed to the widow of Sarepta and Naaman the Syrian, and he held up the men of Nineveh as a rebuke (Matthew 12:41).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jesus rebuked Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum and spoke often of Jerusalem (Matthew 11:21-23).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The good Samaritan story runs from Jerusalem down to Jericho, and Jesus named Samaria as a mission field (Luke 10:30; Acts 1:8).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Jesus said Tyre and Sidon would have repented, and told of the widow of Sarepta (Matthew 11:21; Luke 4:26).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jesus said the men of Nineveh would rise in judgment against his generation (Matthew 12:41).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: At Nazareth Jesus recalled Naaman the Syrian (Luke 4:27).

prompts.display_text: Pin an island country or territory (Australia excluded; Japan, UK and Philippines count) with a Church stake as of October 2026.
prompts.text_original: An island country or territory (Australia and Hawaii excluded; Japan, the United Kingdom and the Philippines count) where the Church has at least one stake as of October 2026.
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (figures of 31 Dec 2025), read 4 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Islands hold some of the Church's strongest stake networks: the Philippines (141), the United Kingdom (41), New Zealand (28), Japan (22), the Dominican Republic (22), Tonga (21) and Samoa (20). Smaller island stakes stretch from Ireland and Cape Verde to Bahrain, Madagascar, Jamaica and Micronesia. Iceland, Malta, Cyprus, Sri Lanka, Cuba and Mauritius have no stake.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose language received a full triple combination (three books of scripture in one) between 2000 and 2019.
prompts.text_original: After the Book of Mormon, a language's next milestone is usually a triple combination: the Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price in one volume. Pin a country whose Church chronology records its language's triple combination arriving between 2000 and 2019.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Albania, Armenia, Cambodia, Kiribati, Lithuania, Malaysia, Zimbabwe, Ukraine
prompts.summary: A triple combination gathers the Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price in one volume. Between 2000 and 2019 languages gaining one included Albanian (2004), Ukrainian (2005), Armenian and Lithuanian (2006), Khmer and Shona (2007), Kiribati (2017) and Malay (2018).

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: The Albanian triple combination was published August 11, 2004.

answers.name: Armenia
answers.fact: The Armenian triple combination arrived for distribution in August 2006.

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: Khmer Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price were published in July 2007 with a triple combination.

answers.name: Malaysia
answers.fact: The triple combination was translated into Malay in March 2018.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: The Shona triple combination was published in 2007.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: The Church announced the publication of the Kiribati-language triple combination on September 28, 2017.

answers.name: Lithuania
answers.fact: The Lithuanian triple combination was published in September 2006.
